findings.body: This fallback promotes both task children and fixes using `_green_at`, which checks only configured names (board.py:528–539). With required checks successful but another check failed or running, the row therefore reports `stage: ready` alongside `pr.checks: fail/running`; close's actual gate rejects those results (checks.py:35–50). It also restores readiness after a new branch commit invalidates the receipt: the queried `headRefOid` is never compared with the branch head, so even a freshly fetched green result for the previous pushed commit makes the new local commit appear ready. These are additional cases beyond the previous successful-required-check repair. The regression at tests/test_machine_views.py:414–418 supplies no successful GraphQL rollup and misses this bypass. Require a complete passing result for the current head, and keep the item's next-step explanation consistent.
findings.title: Not done: derive readiness from the current head's complete check result

findings.body: The previously reported issue remains: `release_notice` prepends the newer-release announcement (upgrade.py:168–188), and `machine_next` selects the first non-Next line. Consequently, `forge next --json` returns the release announcement as `next.line`, hiding the actual waiting or human-only merge state when `next.command` is null. Build the machine next object from `_report`'s lines and keep any release notice separate.
findings.title: Keep release notices from replacing next.line
